title: Playing advertising wagons and Wild West show corners
summary: Laine recalls advertising wagons for fights, balls and football, a clarinetist's torn pants story, and playing on corners near a Wild West show.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you play much, uh, jobs as advertising? Do much advertising? Plenty.

Fights and balls and stuff like that. Oh yeah, plenty. Plenty advertising wagons for fights and balls and stuff like that. You know. Advertising wagons for football players too. You know, for game football players and all that sort of stuff. Yeah, played lots of advertising wagons. Plenty of them. I'll never forget the day that I played for the, um, John Ruskin Segoe advertisement on Canal Street. I had a fellow by the name of Fisher who was playing clarinet. He, it was some kind of a, a nail or something on the side of the, uh, advertisement banner. They ripped his pants all the way down. And the guy that's seen that, you know, he said, I don't know what you're worried. He says, wrote him out a little note. He says, come and see me. Bought him a whole shoot of clothes. Just put that shoot, that rip down there.
That's that. Bought him a whole shoot of clothes.
Would, would you play those advertisements by, in one particular spot or would you?

No, all around, all around town. On a wagon? Yes. All around town. Well, not, not, not standing nowhere at all. Now, like I said, we played, uh, Wild West show where we played at, stand on the corner. Uh-huh. See, at nights, at nights, before the show. See?
Near to where the show was?
It's on the corner. But then she said the show was in the middle of this block here. We played either corner. Uh-huh. See? And then today, we'd advertise the show in a wagon. Mm-hmm.
